properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, dev_reflow2 hub session, 2026-09-27, in the same breath as settling the design-and-export rules:

"we should explore how to share designs at some brainstorm (my brother was thinking emails and I was thinking just click share https://api.flo2.io/g/54ae4a4f0b458b77/mcp, for instance. that's obviously for flo2, so this opens a question for how does somebody share a reflow2 design - probably just using the standard export design, which we termed "photocopy")."

THE FRAME, from the accepted rules (dec:idea-one-blueprint-the-store-is-the-design-and-an-export-is-a-perishable-photocopy): rule 2 says sharing IS shared access to the server that holds the design, and rule 5 says an export taken to another server is a FORK. So there are two different acts, and the options below fall into one or the other:
- SHARING: two people work ONE design on one server.
- HANDING OVER: someone gets their OWN copy and it diverges from then on.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══
(a) CLICK SHARE, GET THE ADDRESS (Anthony). The design's own address, e.g. https://api.flo2.io/g/54ae4a4f0b458b77/mcp. That is sharing, on a server that gives each design an address. The address alone grants nothing: the server must also let the other person in. On flo2 that is a membership; flo2's own brainstorm is flo2's dec:idea-choose-which-account-to-share-a-design-with (in flo2's design), whose option (c) is this share link.
(b) INVITE BY EMAIL (Alex, relayed by Anthony). The owner types the other person's email address, and the server lets that person in when they sign in. That is sharing. It needs an account system, which flo2 has and reflow2 deliberately does not (dec:idea-authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer-and-the-line-is-the-contributor-id). flo2's brainstorm lists it as option (b), and Anthony said on 2026-09-24 it is the picker he would use.
(c) SEND THE EXPORT (Anthony's guess for reflow2 without flo2). The standard export, by any means (email attachment, a file share). By rule 5 this is HANDING OVER, not sharing. The receiver imports it into their own server and has their own design from then on. It is a real use case (give someone a design to run separately) and it needs no server in common.
(d) A SHARED reflow2 SERVER WITHOUT flo2. An organisation runs its own reflow2 server (the case Alex's workplace raised, req:a-local-client-works-against-a-remote-reflow2-server-by-url) and hands out its address. That is sharing. Who may reach which design is the operator's front layer, not reflow2's.

═══ WHAT THIS SUGGESTS reflow2 ITSELF OWES (a finding, not a choice) ═══
- For SHARING, reflow2's part is small: a design's address as something a person can hand over, and a client that attaches to it (the pointer file, dec:idea-a-checkout-knows-which-remote-design-it-implements, settled and unbuilt). Letting someone in is the server operator's: flo2's memberships, or an organisation's own layer.
- For HANDING OVER, reflow2's part is the export and saying plainly that it is one: the design-and-export decision's open question (d), a stamp such as "taken from <server>/<id> at <time>; a fork from here, not tracked". The receiver's import must know it is starting a new design, not updating a shared one.

═══ PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT ═══
· AN EXPORT SENT BY EMAIL CAN LOOK LIKE SHARING when it is not. Two people each import the same export and both think they are "on the design". A week later there are two designs. The stamp in (d) is what keeps that visible.
· AN ADDRESS WITHOUT A GRANT IS A DEAD LINK, and one WITH a public grant is a leak. Whatever carries the share must carry who it was meant for (flo2's membership, an email), not only where.
· cure's content is private (a personal medical project). Whatever sharing lands must default to nobody.
properties.name: OPEN — how does somebody share a reflow2 design: hand over its address, invite by email, or send an export (which is a fork, not a share)?
